B. 2 Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 25 (print p. 154), VI.A.3.

content.sourcePart: Part A: Sample Questions by BoK
content.stem: Which of the following probability distributions has negative values?
content.why: Among the choices, only the Student’s t distribution has negative values. B. Student’s t Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part A III. Measure Phase, Question 34 (print p. 53), III.C.

content.sourcePart: Part A: Sample Questions by BoK
content.stem: Find the area under the standard normal curve between 1.00 standard deviation and 2.50 standard deviations from the mean.
content.why: Using a standard normal table, P(1.00 < Z < 2.50) = P(Z < 2.50) − P(Z < 1.00) = 0.99379 − 0.84134 = 0.15245, which rounds to 0.1524. B. 0.1524 Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part A III. Measure Phase, Question 35 (print p. 54), III.C.

content.sourcePart: Part A: Sample Questions by BoK
content.stem: The weights of soup cans follow a normal distribution with a mean of 16.0 oz and a standard deviation of 0.005 oz. What percentage of cans weigh more than 16.0075 oz?
content.why: The weight variable follows a N(16.0, 0.005²) distribution. To find P(X > 16.0075), we will use the standard normal distribution. Z = (16.0075−16.0) / 0.005 = 1.5. Using a cumulative standard normal table, we find P(Z > 1.5) = 1− P(Z < 1.5) = (1 − 0.9332) = 0.0668 = 6.68%. Note that the standard normal table in Appendix F of The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Handbook gives values for P(Z > z), so the answer can be taken directly from the table. A. 6.68% Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part A III. Measure Phase, Question 36 (print p. 54), III.C.

content.sourcePart: Part A: Sample Questions by BoK
content.why: Using a standard normal table, P(−1.33 < Z < 2.75) = 0.99702 − 0.09176 = 0.90526, which rounds to 0.9053. B. 0.9053 Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part A III. Measure Phase, Question 37 (print p. 54), III.C.

content.sourcePart: Part A: Sample Questions by BoK
content.stem: Find the probability that Z ≥ 0.50.
content.why: To find P(Z ≥ 0.50), we can find 1− P(Z < 0.50) using the standard normal table, in which 1− P(Z < 0.50) = 1− 0.69146 = 0.30854. Note that the standard normal table in Appendix F of The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Handbook gives values for P(Z > z), so the answer can be taken directly from the table. A. 0.3085 Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part A III. Measure Phase, Question 38 (print p. 54), III.C.

Measure Phase, Question 39 (print p. 54), III.C.

content.stem: A factor that is not of experimental interest but is included in the analysis in order to reduce experimental error is known as a(n):
content.why: A blocking variable is not of experimental interest but is included in the analysis to reduce experimental error. D. blocking variable. Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 75 (print p. 165), V.A.1.

content.stem: SDCA stands for:

Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 76 (print p. 165), VI.B.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: A team succeeds in speeding up a process. What might be an unintended negative consequence?
content.why: By concentrating solely on speed, the process might be suboptimized if rework then increases. A. Rework increases. Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 77 (print p. 165), II.C.4.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: Which tool is used for waste elimination?
content.why: Pull systems are a lean tool used for waste elimination. D. Pull systems Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 78 (print p. 166), V.C.1.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: What is the formula for the probability of two events occurring when the events are independent?
content.why: For independent events, P(B|A) = P(B), so the multiplication rule becomes P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B). B. P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B) Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 79 (print p. 166), III.B.1.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: What action can we take on a null hypothesis?
content.why: A null hypothesis can only be rejected or fail to be rejected; it cannot be accepted because of a lack of evidence to reject it. A. Reject or fail to reject Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 7 (print p. 150), IV.B.2.

content.stem: Which statement describes how SMART goals are used in a Six Sigma project?
content.why: SMART goals can keep the team focused to avoid project scope creep. D. They help prevent scope creep across the DMAIC process. Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 80 (print p. 166), I.A.2.

content.stem: Verification and validation are used to compare results against which of the following factors?
content.why: The project’s stated goals are what the verification and validation (V&V) should focus on. Verification is assessment to specifications. Stated goals Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 81 (print p. 166), I.C.1.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: What is a numerical value that provides information about the entire system being studied?
content.why: The entire system being studied is the population. Populations are described using parameters. Samples are described using statistics. A. Parameter Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 82 (print p. 166), III.B.

content.stem: Those who have a vested interest in the process and/or its products and outputs are:

In-depth qualitative insights and group dynamics

content.why: Focus groups excel in providing in-depth qualitative insights by facilitating discussions among participants, allowing exploration of perceptions, opinions, and group dynamics. C. In-depth qualitative insights and group dynamics Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 84 (print p. 167), II.D.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: Calculate the precision-to-tolerance (P/T) ratio using the following information. Specifications: 10 ± 0.5 cm and σtotal = 0.045 cm.
content.why: The P/T ratio is 6σmeasurement divided by the tolerance width: 6(0.045)/(10.5−9.5) = 0.27 = 27%. B. 27% Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 85 (print p. 167), III.E.

the probability of rejecting H0 when it is false.
the probability of accepting H0 when it is true.
content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: In a statistical test, power is defined as:
content.why: Power is 1−β: the probability of rejecting H₀ when H₀ is false. C. the probability of rejecting H0 when it is false. Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 86 (print p. 167), IV.B1.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: A factor that caused a nonconformance and should be permanently eliminated through process improvement is a(n):
content.why: This question asks how to prevent reoccurrences, thus requiring a root cause. A. root cause. Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 87 (print p. 167), IV.C.

content.stem: A c-chart tracks the:
content.why: A c-chart tracks the count of nonconformities. Sample sizes are constant. C. count of nonconformities. Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 88 (print p. 168), VI.A.3.

content.why: Check sheets use pre-categorized potential outcomes for data collection using sets of words, tally lists, or graphics. D. Check sheets Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 8 (print p. 150), III.D.2.

content.why: The specification section of the control plan would provide the requirements for parameters being monitored. A. Specification Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 90 (print p. 168), VI.B.1.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: Place the following flowcharting steps in order, from first to last: 1. Build the sequence of the process. 2. Determine the process steps through brainstorming or walking the process. 3. Draw the flowchart with the appropriate symbols. 4. Create the process boundaries. 5. Verify that the chart is complete.
content.why: The correct sequence is boundaries, identify steps, arrange the sequence, draw the chart, and verify completeness: 4, 2, 1, 3, 5. B. 4, 2, 1, 3, 5 Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 96 (print p. 170), III.A.

content.stem: In a multi-vari chart study, another term for within-part variation is:
content.why: Positional variation is another term for within-part variation. A. positional variation. Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 97 (print p. 170), IV.A.1.

content.stem: np is the mean of which distribution?
content.why: For a binomial random variable, the mean is μ = np. C. Binomial Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 98 (print p. 170), III.C.

content.sourcePart: Part B: Practice Exam
content.stem: To determine the efficacy of a weight loss regimen, participants are weighed at the start and at the end of the 12-week program. Which pair of hypotheses would be most appropriate for this study?
content.why: The same participants are measured before and after, so use paired differences. Defining D = Before−After, an effective program produces μD > 0; test H₀: μD = 0 versus H₁: μD > 0. D. H₀: μD = 0 vs. H₁: μD > 0 Source: The ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt Study Guide (2024), Part B Practice Exam, Question 99 (print p. 171), IV.B.2.
